subject: Re: Stabilizer sunset language & conditional rebate triggers — redline walkthrough
thread_text:
From: Alicia Park <alicia.park@helixdata.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com; marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Ben Cohen <bcohen@helixdata.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HelixData — Order Form redlines (stabilizer / sunset)

Jonas / Marissa —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Attached is HelixData's redline of the proposed order form (Helix_Redline_OrderForm_v3.pdf). Our procurement team is comfortable with most of the standard terms, but there are two sticking points in the pricing exhibits: (1) the temporary rate stabilizer (they want an explicit 12-month sunset tied to usage baselines and (2) the conditional rebate trigger language — they want it tied to quarterly attainment rather than annual true-up.

High level asks:
- Add explicit sunset mechanics and an operational definition for a "stabilizer period" (start/end plus baseline calculation).
- Replace the annual rebate trigger with a quarterly attainment matrix and cap the rebate pool at 5% of paid fees per quarter.
- Clarify invoicing/crediting mechanics so they hit the same fiscal quarter.

Ben (legal) included alternate language in the PDF. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the sunset + quarterly trigger, or propose alternate guardrails that preserve our cost exposure?

Appreciate a redline back by EOD Mon so procurement can move to exec approval.

Best,
Alicia Park
Head of Procurement, HelixData

---
On Wed, 28 Oct 2026 at 09:12 Alicia Park wrote:
> Attachment: Helix_Redline_OrderForm_v3.pdf (redline)

------------------------------------------------------------
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Alicia Park <alicia.park@helixdata.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixData — Order Form redlines (stabilizer / sunset)

Alicia —

Thanks for sending the redline. We reviewed Ben's proposed language and discussed internally with Product and Billing. Two quick callouts:

1) Sunset mechanics: We're open to a finite stabilizer period, but need the baseline math to be operationally deterministic. Our ask: baseline defined as the average of the preceding 3 full months prior to contract effective date, and the sunset window to be expressed as "N months after the stabilizer start date" (we propose 12 months by default). That avoids disputes about partial-month normalization.

2) Quarterly rebate triggers: Quarterly triggers create more churn in our forecasting and increase short-term cost volatility. If HelixData needs quarterly measurement, we can accept it provided: (a) a per-quarter cap of 5% of fees paid that quarter (you requested this), (b) a lookback smoothing where attainment is averaged across the current quarter + prior quarter to reduce edge-case volatility, and (c) an annual true-up to reconcile any over/under credits so accounting aligns.

I've attached a proposed "Sunset Matrix" (RW_Proposed_Sunset_Matrix.xlsx) with examples showing month-by-month invoice impacts. We redlined the order form and included alternate phrasing under Section 3.2 (pricing exhibits).

Two asks for you: 1) confirm Ben's redline on the crediting mechanics (invoice vs. account credit — Ben's note implies they insist on invoice-level credit) and 2) confirm whether Helix can accept the smoothing window so we can reduce billing volatility.

If you prefer, we can do a 30-min redline call Monday morning.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Americas
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RW_Proposed_Sunset_Matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

------------------------------------------------------------
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Alicia Park <alicia.park@helixdata.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixData — Order Form redlines (stabilizer / sunset)

Alicia —

Adding more context from Legal/Finance: we need three guardrails if we move to quarterly rebates:

- Cap the total rebate pool per quarter at 5% of fees paid that quarter (Jonas suggested).
- Implement a minimum usage threshold (10% of baseline) below which no rebate is payable — this protects against extreme dropouts or change of business.
- Define a recovery clause: if Helix re-accelerates usage above baseline within 6 months after a credited quarter, credits may be clawed back proportional to that acceleration (to prevent short-term gaming).

Also, our billing system can only apply invoice-level credits that map to the fiscal quarter in which the rebate is earned; we can't retroactively change prior quarter invoices after 90 days without a manual journal. That is why an annual reconciliation step is important: it captures any edge case rounding or over-crediting and preserves your accounting cadence.

If Helix insists on purely quarterly settlement without annual true-up, we will need to reflect that as a higher per-quarter reserve (we would model that into pricing).

Happy to jump on a call to walk the language live.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

------------------------------------------------------------
From: Ben Cohen <bcohen@helixdata.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com; jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Alicia Park <alicia.park@helixdata.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 14:45:00 -0500
Subject: RE: HelixData — Order Form redlines (stabilizer / sunset)

Laura / Jonas —

Thanks for the detailed response. A couple clarifications from Helix legal:
- The minimum usage threshold is acceptable but would prefer 5% rather than 10% — Helix is contracting to move a portion of their workload to Redwood and wants the threshold to be reasonable.
- The clawback language: Helix can't accept a broad 6-month clawback tied to any re-acceleration — they would consider a proportionate clawback only if the acceleration is the result of incremental workload that was not contemplated in the baseline (we proposed a carveout tied to newly deployed product lines).
- Regarding the annual true-up: Helix is flexible on an annual true-up, but they want the default settlement to be quarterly cash/credit applied in the quarter earned. They understand reconciliation is needed for bookkeeping but want primary remediation to be timely.

Ben attached the redline PDF showing alternative wording for clawback and a suggestion to set minimum threshold to 5%.

Would Redwood consider: minimum threshold 5%, quarter-level settlement with auto annual true-up only if cumulative credits exceed 3% of annual paid fees? That reduces low-value true-ups while keeping Helix's preference for timelier settlement.

Thanks,
Ben Cohen
Senior Counsel, HelixData
Attachment: Helix_Redline_OrderForm_v3.pdf (redline)

------------------------------------------------------------
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Alicia Park <alicia.park@helixdata.com>, Ben Cohen <bcohen@helixdata.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixData — Order Form redlines (stabilizer / sunset)

Ben / Alicia —

Appreciate the constructive counterproposal. Summary of where Redwood can land today without pricing re-model:

1) Stabilizer sunset: accept a 12-month stabilizer window with baseline = avg of the 3 full months prior to effective date. Language will include the normalization rule for partial months.

2) Minimum threshold: agree to 5% (reduced from our ask) to reflect Helix's migration plan.

3) Quarterly settlement + annual true-up: we can operate on quarter-level credits applied in the quarter earned. We will keep the annual true-up as a reconciliation step, but will only trigger a journal/adjustment if cumulative annual credits exceed 3% of annual paid fees (your suggested threshold). For any smaller deltas, we will net on next invoice to avoid manual journals.

4) Clawback: accept a narrower clawback focused on incremental workloads explicitly excluded from the baseline (your carveout). We will include a defined notice process and a joint review window before any clawback is applied.

Next steps:
- I'll circulate a clean updated Order Form with the agreed language and mark the strike-throughs for the few remaining points (target EOD Tue).
- Marissa / Karthik: please confirm the billing-side feasibility of the 3% annual true-up threshold and the invoice netting behavior so I can pass a final operational note to Ben.

If that all checks out, Alicia can present to her execs next week. Happy to take a final 20-minute alignment call if helpful.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Americas
Redwood Inference

Attachment: OrderForm_clean_v2.pdf (clean copy with updated clauses)
